newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australis says sport pull overrated.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australis says sport pull overrated.

text.p: Australis Media Ltd chief executive Sean O'Halloran said on Wednesday he believed sports programming was overrated as a driving force behind pay television subscription levels in Australia.
"Sport has been over-estimated in the market as a driver. I think that movies are frankly broadly equivalent," O'Halloran told reporters after the company's annual meeting.
O'Halloran said the general entertainment package that Australis offered through its Galaxy pay television service was far superior to its competition, Foxtel and Optus Vision.
Foxtel is jointly owned by News Corp Ltd and government-owned telecommunications group Telstra Corp.
Optus Vision is 46.5 percent owned each by Optus Communications Pty Ltd and Continental CableVision, which is currently merging with U.S. West Communications Group.

O'Halloran said one of the reasons sport was overrated was because the commercial networks had a stranglehold on the free to air television and pay television rights for sport in Australia due partly to anti-syphoning rules.

Earlier, Australis chairman Mark Johnson told the annual meeting the company would be introducing new products and ideas to increase the number of channels and the choice available to subscribers following further deregulation of the industry.
In August Australis announced a joint venture agreement to share DTH satellite infractructure with Optus Vision.

At the same time Australis announced a consortium involving Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Lenfest Communications Inc would provide the company with US$105 million of equity finance.
The deals were approved by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission in October.
"Significant cost reductions and funding benefits are expected to flow to the company from the arrangements," Johnson said.
At 11.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), Australis shares were steady at 15 cents.
